value.text: It may not be in your best interest to replace existing life insurance policies or annuity contracts in connection with the purchase of a new life insurance policy, whether issued by the same or different insurance company. A replacement will occur if, as part of your purchase of a new life insurance policy, existing coverage has been, or is likely to be, lapsed, surrendered, forfeited, assigned, terminated, changed or modified into paid-up insurance or other forms of benefits, loaned against or withdrawn from, reduced in value, by use of cash values or other policy values, changed in the length of time or in the amount of insurance that would continue or continued with a stoppage or reduction in the amount of premium paid. Prior to completing a replacement transaction, you may want to contact the insurance company or agent who sold you the life insurance or annuity contract that will be replaced to help you decide whether the replacement is in your best interest.

wording.defaultText:
AUTHORIZATION:  
I authorize any licensed physician, medical practitioner, hospital, pharmacy, clinic or other medical or medically related facility, laboratory, insurance company, MIB, LLC. ("MIB"), or other organization, institution or person, that has any records or knowledge of me or my health to release information, including prescription drug records, maintained by physicians, pharmacy benefit managers, and other sources of information to New York Life Insurance Company, its reinsurers, its subsidiaries or the plan administrator about the physical and mental health of any persons proposed for insurance, including significant history, findings, diagnosis and treatment, but excluding psychotherapy notes for the purpose of evaluating my application for insurance. Health information obtained will not be re-disclosed without my authorization unless permitted by law, in which case it may not be protected under federal privacy rules. For example, New York Life may be required to provide it to insurance, regulatory, or other government agencies. In this case, the information may no longer be protected by the rules governing your AUTHORIZATION.

A photocopy of this AUTHORIZATION and request form shall be as valid as the original. In all circumstances, my authorized agent, representative, or I may request a copy of this AUTHORIZATION. This AUTHORIZATION may be used for a period of 24 months from the date signed, unless sooner revoked.  The AUTHORIZATION may be revoked at any time by sending written notice to New York Life Insurance Company. My revocation will not be effective to the extent that New York Life or any other person already has disclosed or collected information or taken other action in reliance on it, or to the extent that New York Life has a legal right to contest a claim under an insurance certificate or the certificate itself.

As used in the Statement of Health the medical questions above:

 “Bloodborne pathogen” means pathogenic microorganisms that are present in human blood and can cause disease in humans. These pathogens  include,  but  are  not  limited  to,  hepatitis  B  virus  (HBV),  hepatitis  C  virus  (HCV),  and  human  immunodeficiency  virus  (HIV).  

“Emergency medical services person” means an individual employed or receiving compensation to provide out-of-hospital emergencymedical  services  such  as  a  firefighter,  paramedic,  emergency  medical  technician,  licensed  nurse,  rescue  squad  person,  or  other  individual who serves as an employee or volunteer of an ambulance service or a member of an organized first responder squad that is formally  recognized  by  a  political  subdivision  in  the  state,  who  provides  out-of-hospital  emergency  medical  services  during  theperformance of the individual’s duties, an individual employed as a licensed peace officer, a crime laboratory worker while working outside the laboratory and involved in criminal investigation, an individual who renders emergency care or assistance at the scene of an emergency, or while an injured person is being transported to receive medical care and who is acting as a good Samaritan, and any individual who, in the process of executing a citizens’ arrest, may have experienced a significant exposure to a source individual.

 “Source individual” means an individual, living or dead, whose blood, tissue, or potentially infectious body fluids may be a source of bloodborne  pathogen  exposure  to  an  emergency  medical  service  person.  Examples  include,  but  are  not  limited  to,  a  victim  of  an  accident, injury, or illness, or a deceased person.

"Significant exposure” means contact likely to transmit a bloodborne pathogen, in a manner supported by the most current guidelines and recommendations of the United States Public Health Service at the time an evaluation takes place, that includes: (1) percutaneous injury,  contact  of  mucous  membrane  or  nonintact  skin,  or  prolonged  contact  of  intact  skin;  and  (2)  contact,  in  a  manner  that  may transmit a bloodborne pathogen, with blood, tissue, or potentially infectious body fluids.

AUTHORIZATION:  I authorize physicians, practitioners, hospitals, clinics or medically related facilities, pharmacies, pharmacy benefit managers, laboratories, insurance companies, MIB, LLC (“MIB”), medical information retrieval services, electronic health record companies or health care information technology companies to  release to New York Life Insurance Company or New York Life Insurance and Annuity Corporation (collectively “New York Life”), its reinsurers, or the plan administrator at New York Life’s expense, whether in electronic or paper form, information they may have about my physical or mental health, my prescription drug history, diagnostic testing  and copies of my drug and alcohol records, including my records relating to substance abuse education, prevention, training, treatment, rehabilitation or research. This also may include information on the diagnosis, treatment, and testing results related to HIV, AIDS, and sexually transmitted diseases, unless otherwise restricted by state law. Mental health professionals may provide their records, excluding psychotherapy notes, of my diagnosis, functional status, treatment plan, symptoms, prognosis, progress to date, medication prescription and monitoring, and clinical test results for the purpose of evaluating my application for insurance. This includes protected health information and any health information I have previously requested be withheld from further disclosure, and including my history, their findings, diagnoses and treatment.

MIB, other insurance companies, any employers, financial institutions, and consumer reporting agencies may provide to New York Life at New York Life’s expense data about: my driving record; my financial information; any criminal activity; hazardous sport or aviation activity; use of alcohol or drugs; any claim of eligibility for disability income benefits; other applications for insurance; and other policies of insurance. New York Life may obtain an investigative consumer report about me. 

A photocopy of this AUTHORIZATION and request form shall be as valid as the original.  My authorized agent or representative, or I may request a copy of this AUTHORIZATION. This AUTHORIZATION may be used for a period of 24 months from the date signed, unless sooner revoked as stated in the Important Notice.  The AUTHORIZATION may be revoked at any time by sending written notice to New York Life. My revocation will not be effective to the extent that New York Life or any other person already has disclosed or collected information or taken other action in reliance on it, or to the extent that New York Life has a legal right to contest a claim under an insurance certificate or the certificate itself.

I understand and agree that:
•	New York Life may use the information obtained by this AUTHORIZATION to determine my eligibility for insurance, to evaluate a claim for benefits, to contest coverage, or for reinsurance or other insurance purposes, including development of new products and services.
•	To obtain the data described above, New York Life may give my personal information to the above persons or organizations. 
•	New York Life may give data collected about me to: its subsidiaries; affiliates; parent company; agents and their staffs; organizations that perform business functions for it; reinsurers, and others as permitted or required by law. 
•	The medical information New York Life obtains through this AUTHORIZATION may no longer be subject to federal laws and regulations that apply to an individual’s protected health information (the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule). The information New York Life obtains through this AUTHORIZATION may become subject to further disclosure.
•	Authorizing the disclosure of this health information is voluntary. 
•	I can refuse to sign this AUTHORIZATION. However, failure to execute this AUTHORIZATION may result in New York Life being unable to collect information relating to me and result in denial of my application for insurance.

definition.behavior: Next and Back use the form-flow resolver and skip pages whose display conditions evaluate to false.

Pages can register an onBeforeNext hook that pauses forward navigation, shows an intermediate step (e.g. a confirmation dialog or send dialog), and resumes navigation only when the page calls the provided continueNavigation callback. Used by Coverage (dependent-only confirmation) and Profile (advisor send dialog).
If Beneficiary or Payment is configured as none, the page is skipped from the active form flow.

Beneficiary requires a requested amount and an applicant/product allowed by the captured beneficiary participation policy, unless the page is configured as none. The shared fallback gate selects Life (LI) or Accidental Death (AD); explicit Site, Association and applicant exceptions remain authoritative.

Shown for an active applicant whose resolved health page is health-si, falling back to the captured SI gate when no health-page override exists. Assigned source questionnaires may supersede this page.
Shown when a Whole Life product with SI and UW flow is selected.

Health TELE resolves the active adult LI/DI/CI questionnaire from effective product and processing policies. Health DI SUPP is a separate explicitly participating supplemental questionnaire; assigned combined TELE policies can supersede it.

Shown when the captured CIR rider gate matches an enabled rider selection and the page participates in the Site flow. WAEPA's dedicated CIR questionnaire retains its separately approved provisional deferral.

Shown for an active applicant whose resolved health page is health-qd, falling back to the captured QD gate when no health-page override exists. Assigned source questionnaires may supersede this page.
Shown when LI (QD) is selected with a CIR rider.
Multiple routed health pages are presented within the consolidated application-review/progress experience rather than as separate major progress stages.
If every page in a progress stage is skipped, the stage is removed from the active progress steps.
After Review is submitted, Back navigation is disabled on pages after Review.

definition.rule: Back button hidden with no previous page
definition.behavior: The PageHeader/PageTitle back arrow is rendered only when getPreviousFormPageId resolves a previous page for the current values and the page is not after a submitted review; otherwise the back control is hidden, including on post-review pages after submission.

definition.rule: Single template embeds the application in landing-page sections
definition.behavior: template=single embeds SinglePageApplication below the landing content. SinglePageSections renders the active applicant page within a vertical progress layout; completing a page advances to the next applicable section, and permitted edits reopen earlier sections. Shared page participation, validation and routing rules still apply. The theme also forces narrow-screen layout for md/lg/xl responsive styles.

definition.rule: sm breakpoint stays real so sm-level padding isn't lost
definition.behavior: forceMobileLayout only overrides md/lg/xl — sm (600px) is left at its default. Components that only bump padding/spacing at sm (e.g. FormRoutePage's FormShell, which uses px: { xs: 2, sm: "48px" }) still receive that breathing room once the real browser viewport is 600px or wider, instead of staying pinned to their tightest xs padding on an actual desktop screen.

definition.rule: Single template places the application below the landing content
definition.behavior: In single template, Home renders the configured landing content followed by SinglePageApplication. The application reuses the existing applicant page components within one vertical section layout. Artwork follows the configured single-page artwork setting; a fixed hero/form width is not an independent business rule.
Field validation failure blocks advancement, shows an error and scrolls toward the first invalid field. Page-level validation failure blocks advancement, shows its message and scrolls to the top.
Current page values are written to shared application state on submit, Back, and unmount when the page was not explicitly saved.

After forward navigation, the destination page displays a Progress Saved snackbar (AppSnackbar, severity=success). The snackbar appears at top-center on large screens and bottom-center on small screens.

When Child is offered and selected and the effective child mode is details, DynamicList collects the fields and saved-answer bindings in the fresh-start children collection. Effective Site field inclusion determines additional questions, including full-time student. Add/Edit validates the record; Eligibility Next requires at least one valid record within the effective maximum, including restored rows. Notice-only mode displays the section note once without collecting or requiring records.
If Spouse is selected, spouse name details must be provided before continuing.
When the Child dependent section is visible, an info alert under the section header states that only unmarried children are eligible for coverage.

When a recognizable ZIP/postal code is entered, the state/province field is automatically derived when a matching configured option exists. The user may manually override the derived state at any time; a subsequent ZIP change will re-derive state from the new ZIP.

Dependent choices follow covered people and effective authored option exclusions, where configured. An exclusion removes its offered choice before the form renders; an unoffered person cannot reveal a dependent section through a retained answer. These presentation rules remain separate from applicant and product eligibility policies. ASCE assigns no additional conditional exclusions.

definition.rule: Category selection and two-step product reveal
definition.behavior: The user first selects one or more coverage categories via a multi-select chip list. Selecting a category may surface additional required questions (tobacco use, income, hours). When all required questions are answered, a 'See my coverage options' button appears. Clicking it validates the form and, if valid, reveals the product catalog. Changing a category selection or question answer after products are shown collapses the catalog and requires another click.

Each product card lists eligible applicants (member, spouse, child) as checkboxes. Checking an applicant reveals a benefit amount dropdown. DI/OO products also show waiting period and max benefit period dropdowns. Optional riders appear as checkboxes; selecting a rider with an amount range reveals a rider amount dropdown. Coverage selections and amounts are stored per product/applicant key.

If only spouse and/or child are selected for all chosen products (no member selection), clicking Next triggers the onBeforeNext hook and opens a ConfirmationDialog. The user must click Continue to proceed or Cancel to stay on Coverage.

The effective Site selects the shared additional-coverage or total-coverage message through coverage-increase-note. This setting changes only the displayed message. Eligibility, allowed amounts, benefit calculations, verified in-force deductions, maxima and validation remain governed by their independent product/applicant policies.

definition.behavior: When the user selects their very first product from a state of no selections, the Coverage added AppDrawer opens to show the full cart. For all subsequent product or applicant additions, a compact 'Added' success AppSnackbar appears instead of re-opening the drawer.
The application header shows the coverage cart on application pages except Home and Receipt, and hides it after Review has been submitted.
The cart icon displays a badge count derived from current coverage selections.

definition.rule: Inline cart hidden until a product is selected
definition.behavior: The 'Your requested coverage' inline panel below the Coverage page product catalog shows nothing at all — no section title and no empty-state placeholder — until at least one applicant has an amount selected for a product (grandTotal > 0). The full-drawer cart variant (opened from the header cart icon or the Coverage page's own summary drawer) is unaffected and still shows its 'No coverage selected yet.' empty state.

definition.rule: Quote reveal mirrors Coverage page's category reveal
definition.behavior: Clicking 'See my quote' validates the category-level fields, reveals the matching product cards, and scrolls the drawer so the revealed products land at the top. The 'See my quote' button then hides and reappears only if the user edits a coverage question (gender, tobacco use, income, hours, business expenses/responsibility) or toggles a coverage category selection — the same show/hide contract as the Coverage page's 'See my coverage options' button.

definition.rule: Estimated cost panel uses the shared TotalCostSummary component
definition.behavior: The quote drawer's estimated cost panel now renders via the same TotalCostSummary component used on the Coverage page and in the coverage cart drawer, instead of a bespoke box. Like the Coverage page's inline cart, the panel is hidden entirely until at least one product/applicant has been added (no 'Added coverage will appear here' placeholder); the rate-frequency toggle and Apply button remain visible whenever products are shown.

Apply requires at least one selected product and revalidates the currently applicable quote answers, eligibility facts, benefit amounts and coverage options. Invalid input stays in the quote with an error; membership is collected later. On success, the canonical quote.apply transition initializes the application with collected eligibility and coverage answers, including tobacco follow-ups, contextual employment facts, selected products/applicants, amounts and selected member riders with their amounts. Coverage shows the carried answers as editable values. Home is the only quote entry point; Membership has no quote helper.
AppSnackbar appears at top-center on large screens and bottom-center on small screens. Used for Progress Saved and Coverage Added feedback.

The shared ConditionalGroup presents configured child fields when the controlling condition is satisfied and collapses them when it is no longer satisfied. Field and section definitions own the controlling conditions and follow-up membership.
Member/spouse health sections follow applicant-applying visibility; the member section label is hidden for member-only flow.

Each health question is a required Yes/No radio. Selecting Yes reveals a DynamicList inline below that question where the user can add one or more detail records (onset date, condition/medication details, physician/hospital address) via the standard Add/Edit/Remove modal pattern. Selecting No collapses and clears the list for that question.
When Payment mode is optional, the page first asks whether the user wants to add payment information; No permits continuation without payment questions.
When payment questions are active, each applicable product requires a payment method and payment frequency before continuing.
Bank-account details (name on account, institution, routing number, account number, authorization checkbox) are displayed when Bank account is selected as the payment method for any product.

AppDrawer slides in from the right on desktop (420–480px wide) or up from the bottom on mobile (75vh). Used for contextual help topics (PageHelpChips → AppDrawer), the QuickDecision℠ explainer, the Coverage Portfolio (TPA-verified users on Coverage), and the application menu sub-drawers (coverage options, needs calculator, QD explainer). Drawers are read-only and do not block page submission.
The swipeable prop enables SwipeableDrawer on mobile for user-initiated drawers (e.g. the Coverage cart drawer). Non-swipeable drawers use a standard Drawer.

DynamicList is the shared component for any repeatable record set (children, insurance companies, health detail records). Existing records render as bordered DynamicListItem cards with Edit and Remove buttons. Add opens an AppModal titled 'Add [Label]' with a blank form. Edit opens the same modal pre-filled with the selected record. Save appends or updates the record. Remove shows a confirmation AppModal ('Remove [Label]?') and deletes on confirm. Fields inside the modal are defined per record type via a mapping prop and rendered by FieldRenderer. The Add button is hidden once maxItems is reached (default 10).
Default displays the inline Quote Tool when Site rates and quoting are available, otherwise the hero image. A Site can select the hero image even when rates are available.
Home displays the saved-application resume prompt/link.

The app header hides when the user scrolls down (threshold: 8px) and reappears immediately on any upward scroll. Implemented via MUI useScrollTrigger + Slide direction='down'. The header uses position='sticky' so it participates in document layout rather than overlapping content.
Application header supports Chat (when enabled and eligible), Coverage Cart and Menu. It does not contain a Quote action in the latest source.
The Chat and Coverage Cart header actions are hidden once ApplicationSessionContext reports that review was submitted, in addition to being hidden on the Home and Receipt pages.

CookieDialog is shown as a fixed bottom banner on first visit. AppShell checks localStorage.cookieConsent !== 'accepted' to decide whether to render it; dismissing sets localStorage.cookieConsent = 'accepted' so it never reappears.
AppBody patches window.history.pushState/replaceState and listens for popstate to track the current pathname, then scrolls the window to top on every route change.

FieldRenderer live-formats input as the user types based on field.format: currency ('$1,234'), percent, phone (parenthesized area code), ssn (dashes, with all but the most-recently-typed digit masked for ~800ms), and month-year. The date input type is also formatted inline.

definition.rule: Auto label variant for long labels
definition.behavior: FieldRenderer auto-selects a 'standard' (external) label instead of the default 'floating' label when field.label is 40+ characters, to avoid clipping, unless field.labelVariant is explicitly set.
Phone-format fields render an inline Mobile/Home/Business type selector tied to a sibling field (field.phoneTypeFieldId, default '<field.id>-type'), unless field.showPhoneTypeSelector is false.

definition.rule: Auto search-select for long option lists
definition.behavior: FieldRenderer renders a field configured as inputType: 'dropdown' using the searchable-select (MUI Autocomplete) component instead of a plain Select once field.options has 10 or more entries, so long lists (e.g. US states) are searchable rather than requiring a long scroll. Fields already explicitly set to 'searchable-select' are unaffected.

definition.rule: Panel page/drawer variant with nested sub-drawers
definition.behavior: HowApplyingWorksPanel and CoverageOptionsPanel accept a variant: 'page' | 'drawer' prop rendering the same content as a full page section or a compact drawer layout. In 'drawer' variant, HowApplyingWorksPanel manages its own nested sub-drawer state (Application Review / QuickDecision℠) stacked above the parent drawer; in 'page' variant those links call parent-supplied handlers instead.

Menu provides Continue Saved Application, How Applying Works, About Coverage, Needs Calculator, About QuickDecision and client Contact information. Each tool closes the main menu drawer and opens a standalone AppDrawer (How Applying Works and About Coverage render HowApplyingWorksPanel / CoverageOptionsPanel in 'drawer' variant).
When Spouse is selected as a dependent, display the applicant-specific spouse sections and fields; post-Coverage applicant selection gates still apply separately.

definition.rule: Revalidate saved applications after Library revision changes
definition.behavior: A recovered or locally remembered save whose Library revision differs requires explicit Coverage or Review completion before mock submission. Ordinary autosaves do not clear that state. The save service and applicant submission check own this client-assisted mock behavior; no warning banner is required.

definition.rule: Product eligibility and benefit limits use captured policies
definition.behavior: Product eligibility constraints, scoped Association eligibility, additional eligibility facts, structured amount assignments, benefit policies and selection/dependent policies own their respective decisions. Explicit Site/product/Association/applicant assignments determine applicability. Association residency lists and identifier roles use their dedicated captured policies. This record references those owners; individual requirements still need semantic coverage verification.

definition.rule: Billing and premium modifiers use captured product policies
definition.behavior: Captured product rate modifier policies and journey billing policies own membership adjustments, billing factors and applicable fees. The rating and billing resolvers execute them; rule prose does not supply competing values.

flagDefinitions.name: Site has product rates
flagDefinitions.description: When false, all rate displays must be hidden; enforced by rule.

flagDefinitions.name: Site product rates are in PRASE
flagDefinitions.description: Site product rates are in PRASE

flagDefinitions.name: Site offers QD
flagDefinitions.derivation: True when at least one enabled product supports QD.

flagDefinitions.name: Applicant applying for QD
flagDefinitions.derivation: True when selected product/path is QD for applicant.

flagDefinitions.name: Product has QD

flagDefinitions.name: Application has underwritten coverage
flagDefinitions.derivation: True for selected member/spouse Life, Disability or Office Overhead; false for child-only Life or only AD&D/HI.

definition.title: Consumer Application Flow
definition.intro: Follow the application stages. Open a stage to see its pages, branches and links to shared processes. Effective Site configuration and selected coverage determine which pages participate.

definition.title: Advisor-Assisted Flow
definition.intro: The advisor prepares the application through Profile, then the applicant verifies access and completes Review, applicable Health, Payment and DocuSign. Advisor and applicant use their own saved contacts. Access follows the preparation, applicant, signing and submitted stages; only one actor holds the active editing session.

definition.title: Resume & Verification Flow
definition.intro: Recover an application through one-use email-link entry followed by phone verification within a fixed MFA session. Shared request budgets, cooldowns and application locks apply; public responses preserve saved-application privacy.

definition.title: Autosave & Persistence Flow
definition.intro: After successful Membership saving establishes the application, later submitted portal pages validate and save before advancing. Validation, technical errors and session expiry have distinct outcomes. Browser caching and external-provider field-level persistence are separate. Resume links and email delivery use the configured shared lifecycle; no live service is implied.

definition.title: Quote Flow
definition.intro: Available through configured entry points (drawer/modal, not a standalone page). Collects minimum information to determine available products and estimated premiums.

definition.title: TPA Member Verification Flow
definition.intro: Global TPA workflow after Eligibility saves. Effective Site assignments supply integration mode, lookup fields and address requirements; they do not duplicate the graph. Verification and saved approval/portfolio outcomes are distinct. Fictional lookup records, identity questions and Text/Call outcomes simulate provider behavior; no live service or TPA approval executes.

definition.label: Resume Request
definition.description: Applicant requests with their saved email. Advisor Continue first identifies applicant email, then Resume collects the advisor’s own email and phone and matches both to that application’s saved advisor. Public confirmation does not disclose availability.

definition.label: Request Confirmation
definition.description: Show the same confirmation for matching, missing, expired or recovery-locked records. Send only when appropriate. Link-request limit feedback is also identical for matching and missing emails.

definition.label: Resume Link
definition.description: A ten-minute link is not consumed by opening or rendering its landing page. Only the latest unconsumed link is usable.

definition.label: Resume Method
definition.description: Text or Call to the saved phone. Explicit Next atomically consumes the link, starts the fixed MFA session and issues its first code. Back from code entry reuses the same session.

definition.label: Resume Code
definition.description: Enter the six-digit phone code. Separate code and MFA deadlines apply; resends share the application request budget and preserve failed attempts. Display the fixed-session warning without an extension action.

definition.label: Verification Result
definition.description: Correct current code verifies once. Incorrect current codes spend attempts; malformed, expired and recognized replaced codes do not. The third incorrect attempt immediately locks application recovery. MFA session expiry opens the shared Session expired page. Request limits and attempt locks return to initial Resume with their distinct messages.

definition.label: Restored Destination
definition.description: Before signing, ordinary consumer and advisor recovery return to Eligibility; a prepared-application applicant returns to Review. Once signing has started but is unfinished, applicant recovery returns to DocuSign. The service authorizes actor, lifecycle and destination; no query value grants access. Submitted applications cannot recover.

definition.label: Session expired
definition.description: The shared expiration page for application inactivity or the fixed Resume MFA session ending. Link and phone-code expiry remain inline on their own pages.

definition.label: Advisor entry
definition.description: Start collects advisor identity and opens Membership. Continue collects applicant email as the lookup key; it does not authenticate the advisor.

definition.label: Request link (Advisor)
definition.description: Enter the advisor’s own email and phone. Match both to the saved advisor on the application identified by the applicant email. Always give the same public link-sent confirmation.

definition.label: Secure email (Advisor)
definition.description: Send the separate secure link only to the matching saved advisor email; opening the email does not consume its link.

definition.label: Choose Text or Call (Advisor)
definition.description: Delivery-method Next consumes the link and starts MFA, sending the code to the matching saved advisor phone.

definition.label: Verify phone code (Advisor)
definition.description: Verify before restoring answers. Advisor access is allowed before DocuSign, including takeover during the applicant stage. Successful access returns to Eligibility and ends the prior active editing session.

definition.label: Membership
definition.description: Establish saving only after successful Membership submission.

definition.label: Eligibility
definition.description: Complete or revise eligibility details.

definition.label: Coverage
definition.description: Complete coverage selections using effective product policies.

definition.label: Beneficiary
definition.description: Include when the effective mode and selected products apply. Optional mode allows declining to add beneficiaries.

definition.label: Contact
definition.description: Complete member address and applicable spouse or member employer details.

definition.label: Profile
definition.description: Complete the final preparation page; Next opens the send dialog.

definition.label: Send to applicant for review
definition.description: Show applicant name/email. Cancel stays on Profile. Confirm hands control to the applicant; sending or resending does not extend retention.

definition.label: Application sent
definition.description: Show the sent time and original ten-day deletion deadline. Start new application clears the household and retains advisor email, phone and code.

definition.label: Applicant invitation
definition.description: Continue my application opens Resume. This invitation is separate from the secure email link requested next.

definition.label: Request link (Applicant)
definition.description: The applicant enters their own saved email and receives the same public confirmation, whether or not a recoverable application exists.

definition.label: Secure email (Applicant)
definition.description: Applicant opens the separately requested secure link; no answers are restored before phone verification.

definition.label: Choose Text or Call (Applicant)
definition.description: Explicit Next consumes the link and starts the fixed MFA session; send only to the saved applicant phone.

definition.label: Verify phone code (Applicant)
definition.description: Only valid email-link and phone-code proof restores the application. Apply authoritative access stage and destination.

definition.label: Resume destination
definition.description: Before signing, the verified applicant opens Review. After signing has started but is unfinished, return to DocuSign. Submitted applications cannot recover.

definition.label: Review (Applicant)
definition.description: Show advisor-prepared answers and applicant acknowledgements; earlier advisor-completed stages cannot be directly edited. Do not show the redundant locked-steps banner.

definition.label: Request edit
definition.description: Show the saved advisor email. Cancel stays on Review; Send transfers control to the advisor.

definition.label: Edit request sent
definition.description: Confirm the saved advisor recipient; applicant access ends until the advisor resends.

definition.label: Advisor edit email
definition.description: Identify applicant email and request/application dates. Advisor uses Continue, then authenticates using their own saved contacts.

definition.label: Applicable Health pages
definition.description: Only required questionnaires for the selected products/applicants appear. Five shared pages: SI, TELE, QD, DI SUPP and CIR.

definition.label: Payment
definition.description: Include for Required or Optional mode; optional allows declining payment. None skips the page. Collect details and continue to signing.

definition.label: DocuSign
definition.description: Member always signs; applying spouse also signs; no child signature. Starting signing ends advisor access. Incomplete signing resumes here after applicant verification.

definition.label: Receipt
definition.description: All required signatures complete submission and open Receipt. No separate portal submission action. Prototype final image click simulates this boundary without creating signing evidence.

definition.label: Recovery unavailable
definition.description: After submission, expiry or deletion, do not issue recovery links. Preserve the same public confirmation and privacy; do not expose a read-only Receipt through recovery.

definition.label: Applicant pending notification
definition.description: Reminder opens Resume; secure access remains required. Schedule and production delivery belong to the shared notification rules, not a live prototype batch.

definition.label: Advisor pending notification
definition.description: Reminder identifies applicant email for Continue. Advisor cannot reopen once signing starts.

definition.label: Application deletion notification
definition.description: Notify both the saved advisor and applicant when the incomplete application expires at its original retention deadline and is deleted. The applicant is directed to their advisor without an Apply action; the application cannot be resumed.

definition.label: Home
definition.description: Start opens Membership after the optional configured entry notice; dismissing the notice stays on Home. Quote and Continue application use their linked shared flows.

definition.label: Membership
definition.description: Validate membership and applicant contacts. Only successful Membership saving establishes the saved application and starts autosave and its configured notification. Disqualifying membership remains on this page.

definition.label: Eligibility
definition.description: Collect eligibility and dependent information. After validation and successful saving, run the configured TPA flow and return here for its completion before continuing to Coverage.

definition.label: Coverage
definition.description: Collects eligible applicants, products, amounts, riders, and estimated premiums. Available choices and downstream requirements vary by selected coverage and client configuration.

definition.label: Beneficiary
definition.description: Required or Optional participation includes this page when applicable to selected coverage; Optional permits declining designation. None or inapplicability skips to Contact.

definition.label: Contact
definition.description: Collects configured applicant, mailing, business, and spouse contact information.

definition.label: Profile
definition.description: Collects configured personal, employment, financial, existing-coverage, travel, residence, and spouse information.

definition.label: Review
definition.description: Review active answers and applicable notices and consents. Editing returns to the owning participating page; continue after required acknowledgements. Shared validation and saving apply before navigation.

definition.label: Health Routing
definition.description: Run only the configured SI, TELE, QD, DI SUPP and CIR questionnaires for participating applicants and selected products. No applicable health page continues directly to the next participating Payment or signing step. External QD uses the shared prototype image handoff; no live underwriting service is connected.

definition.label: Payment
definition.description: Required or Optional participation includes this page; Optional permits declining payment collection. None skips directly to signing. Active selections govern the payment documents.

definition.label: E-Sign
definition.description: The member and any applying spouse complete the required electronic signatures; children do not sign. All required signatures complete submission and open Receipt. Unfinished signing can return through Resume. The prototype image sequence simulates completion and does not generate signing evidence.

definition.label: Receipt
definition.description: Show the submission reference, coverage decisions, active document actions and configured next steps. The configured Receipt email follows submission. Submitted applications cannot be restored through Resume; document downloads remain explicit prototype placeholders.

definition.label: Membership establishes the application
definition.description: Successful Membership validation and saving starts this lifecycle for consumer and advisor applications. Local browser caching before that point is separate.

definition.label: Validate submitted page
definition.description: Run registered field and page checks on explicit Next. Remain on the current page with field/page feedback when invalid; corrected answers can be submitted again.

definition.label: Correct the current page
definition.description: Preserve answers and show correctable validation on the current page. No save or successful-save feedback occurs until validation succeeds.

definition.label: Save page answers
definition.description: Await the configured page save. Disable repeated Next actions while submitting. External provider field-level saving is outside Portal autosave.

definition.label: Save outcome?
definition.description: Separate confirmed saving, session expiry, service-signaled technical failure and an unsignaled local simulated failure.

definition.label: Continue after confirmed save
definition.description: Show successful-save feedback only after confirmation. Complete any configured page callback, then resolve the next participating page or single-page section with transition feedback.

definition.label: Shared technical Error page
definition.description: A service-signaled technical failure preserves current answers and opens the shared Error page, honoring any specific error-code mapping. No successful-save feedback or special autosave failure alert is shown.

definition.label: Session expired
definition.description: Application inactivity or an expired save session uses the shared expiration page. Recovery follows the shared Resume rules.

definition.label: Entry Point
definition.description: Open from the configured Home quote entry or shared quote tool. Validate the applicable Home entry fields before opening; preserve errors on Home. Membership has no quote helper. Entry fields passed from Home are not repeated in the calculator.

definition.label: Collect Inputs
definition.description: Collect applicable category questions and applicant data using the shared fields. Validate before revealing products; invalid answers stay in the current calculator stage.

definition.label: Calculate Estimates
definition.description: Reveal eligible assigned products and fictional estimates using the shared product/applicant policies. Show loading while calculating and recalculate after selection or amount changes. An empty eligible product set cannot continue to Apply.

definition.label: Product Selection
definition.description: Choose at least one eligible product/applicant combination and its supported amounts and riders. Apply validates applicable questions and selections; errors stay in the calculator.

definition.label: Carry into Application
definition.description: After valid Apply, create a fresh application session, carry applicable quote answers, tobacco answers, products and riders, close the calculator and open Membership. Prior application answers and an expired session deadline are not reused.

definition.label: Close calculator
definition.description: Closing the calculator returns to its containing Home surface without starting an application.

definition.label: Eligibility saved
definition.description: After membership attestation and successful Eligibility validation and page saving, evaluate the effective TPA integration mode.

definition.label: TPA Eligibility Lookup
definition.description: Look up exactly the configured applicant fields and return existing-member and active-coverage facts. Effective Site configuration supplies lookup fields and fictional prototype records; no live lookup executes.

definition.label: Existing member + active coverage?
definition.description: Both conditions must be true to offer LexisNexis identity verification.

definition.label: Regular Application — No Portfolio
definition.description: No existing member or no active coverage in coverage-verification mode: save an unverified, no-portfolio, manual-review outcome and continue to Coverage.

definition.label: Choose Verification Method
definition.description: Choose a configured verification method or skip. The prototype simulates Text/Call outcomes and security questions; it does not deliver an identity-verification code.

definition.label: LexisNexis Security Questions
definition.description: Answer the configured fictional identity questions. The prototype failure answer produces unsuccessful verification; no live identity provider is connected.

definition.label: Verification successful?
definition.description: A completed verification attempt resolves to success or failure.

definition.label: Regular Application — Portfolio Enabled
definition.description: Save verified=true and portfolio=true and the configured auto-approval outcome for downstream processing. Continue to Coverage. This is a saved policy outcome; the prototype performs no real TPA approval.

definition.label: Regular Application — No Portfolio
definition.description: Verification failed, skipped or dismissed: save an unverified, no-portfolio, manual-review outcome and continue to Coverage.

definition.label: Effective TPA mode
definition.description: Use the global mode definition and effective Site assignment. None, coverage-verification and membership-auto-approval have distinct paths.

definition.label: Continue without TPA
definition.description: None performs no lookup or identity verification and enables no portfolio or automatic approval. Continue the application.

definition.label: Existing member?
definition.description: Membership-auto-approval does not perform identity verification or enable a portfolio.

definition.label: New-member outcome
definition.description: Save the new-member automatic-approval outcome without identity verification or portfolio access, then continue to Coverage. Production processing remains external.

definition.label: Existing-member outcome
definition.description: Save the existing-member manual-review outcome without identity verification or portfolio access, then continue to Coverage.

definition.label: Address required first?
definition.description: Use the effective require-address-before-verification assignment.

definition.label: Collect residential address
definition.description: Validate the required residential address before opening the shared MemberVerification dialog. Invalid input remains here.

definition.label: Local simulated save failure
definition.description: A rejected local save without a service incident retains the current form, shared technical-error wording and current answers. Retry uses the same validation/save path; do not introduce a new redirect or a specialized autosave alert.

definition.label: Edit an earlier section
definition.description: The shared edit confirmation returns to the selected owning page after confirmation. Cancel stays on Review. After editing, normal validated saving and configured page order lead back through the application. Advisor-prepared applicants use the separate Advisor request-edit branch.

definition.condition: Code expired/replaced; check or request current code
Phone-code request cooldown or application recovery lock
Matching advisor email and phone; link actually issued
Beneficiary not included or not applicable
Eligible saved application; secure link actually issued
Advisor takeover before signing; authenticate advisor
Advisor takeover before signing; authenticate advisor
Advisor takeover before signing; authenticate advisor

Local failure without a service incident

library.title: Application autosaved
library.description: Lets the applicant know their in-progress application has been saved automatically.
library.whenSent: Sent as soon as Membership is successfully validated, submitted and saved.

library.title: Application submitted
library.description: Confirms the applicant's application was submitted successfully, with coverage decisions and a confirmation number.
library.whenSent: Sent after all required signatures complete and the application is successfully submitted.
library.notes: Applications that include separate application types submitted together will have a separate email and confirmation number sent per application type.

library.title: Application resume request
library.description: Sends a one-time link so someone can verify their email and continue an in-progress application.
library.whenSent: Sent only for an eligible saved application after the applicant email matches, or after Advisor Continue identifies the applicant and the advisor’s own email and phone match the saved advisor. The public request confirmation never reveals whether a link was issued.

library.title: Application pending
library.description: Reminds the applicant to finish an application that's still in progress.
library.whenSent: Sent on days 3, 5, 7, and 9 while the application remains incomplete and has not been successfully submitted.

library.title: Application deleted
library.description: Notifies the applicant that their saved application has expired and been deleted.
library.whenSent: Sent when an incomplete saved application expires and is deleted, ten days after its initial save. Later saves, advisor sending and recovery do not extend that deadline.

library.title: Application sent [advisor]
library.description: Notifies the advisor that an application has been sent to the applicant for signature.
library.whenSent: Sent when the advisor confirms the “Send to applicant” dialog (the advisor Send Confirmation page is reached).

library.title: Application sent [applicant]
library.description: Lets the applicant know their advisor has prepared their application and it's ready to complete and sign.
library.whenSent: Sent when the advisor confirms the “Send to applicant” dialog (the advisor Send Confirmation page is reached).
library.notes: Sent to the applicant, not the advisor — modeled on the Application autosaved email, with the shared administrator contact support section. Technical support appears on pages only.

library.title: Application pending [advisor]
library.description: Reminds the advisor that an application is still awaiting the applicant's signature.
library.whenSent: Sent on days 3, 5, 7, and 9 while the advisor-prepared application remains incomplete and has not been successfully submitted.

library.title: Application edit request [advisor]
library.description: Notifies the advisor that the applicant requested an edit to the application.
library.whenSent: Sent when the applicant confirms Send in the optional Request edit dialog. The following confirmation page acknowledges the request.

library.title: Application submitted [advisor]
library.description: Notifies the advisor that the applicant's application was submitted.
library.whenSent: Sent after all required signatures complete and the application is successfully submitted.

library.title: Application deleted [advisor]
library.description: Notifies the saved advisor that the incomplete application has expired, been deleted and can no longer be resumed.
library.whenSent: Sent when an incomplete advisor-prepared application expires and is deleted, ten days after its initial save. Sending, edits and recovery do not extend that deadline.
library.notes: Uses the shared email renderer and canonical JSON content.

library.title: Application deleted [applicant]
library.description: Notifies the applicant that the advisor-prepared application was deleted and directs them to their advisor, without an Apply button.
library.whenSent: Sent when an incomplete advisor-prepared application expires and is deleted, ten days after its initial save. Sending, edits and recovery do not extend that deadline.
library.notes: Uses the shared email renderer and canonical JSON content.
